review:
This is a documentary that is well-paced, doesn't stay for more than necessary and tells the truth that governments (Russia, in this case) tries to obfuscate. It shows through the lens of Pavel Talankin, a school teacher/videographer/events coordinator of a small town in Russia, how the start of the war with Ukraine starts affecting the day-to-day life of the students, slowly going from teachers having to read from a script Putin's propaganda of war to the classes to war related activities to students to get them more used to, and in cases, ready to go fight.

Although it touches very delicate and serious themes, Pavel's charisma and enthusiasm (which slowly declines as things get more serious) helps keeping things more bearable and watchable.
